children: Oil futures are rising for a second session on renewed concerns about disruption of flows out of the Persian Gulf. "The latest leg higher is being driven primarily by the renewed escalation in tensions between the U.S. and Iran, with traders ignoring the controversial U.S.-Venezuela deal for now," Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com says in a note. "The near-term outlook remains heavily dependent on the supply side." Softer economic data in China and the U.S. point to some moderation in demand, "but oil is relatively demand-inelastic: consumption tends not to fall sharply simply because prices rise." WTI is up 2.6% at $87.96 a barrel and Brent gains 2.2% to $92.48.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
